Subject: New: Activation matrix + tenant affinity for SilverLake pilot

Irene / Tessa / Marissa —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. SilverLake’s pilot steering committee reviewed the flow and they’ve asked for two items to be in the pilot acceptance criteria before we sign the PO: 1) an "activation matrix" that lets us map model behavior to tenant activation tiers (free / standard / enterprise) so we can enforce different generation limits & routing rules per tier, and 2) a tenant affinity mechanism so requests from high-value tenants are routed to a dedicated warm pool (or pinned model variant) to guarantee sub-200ms tail latency for our premium customers.

I’ve attached a short SOW excerpt and a rough activation spreadsheet (activation-matrix-proposal.xlsx) to show the ask. High level timeline expectations from SilverLake: pilot kickoff by May 10, acceptance gates by end of June.

Can Redwood commit to blocking a sprint slot to implement a minimal activation matrix + tenant affinity (even as a config/flag) for pilot? If not, what is the earliest alternate path — e.g., config-based routing + pre-warm shim?

Priya
Head of Product Partnerships
SilverLake AI

Subject: Re: New: Activation matrix + tenant affinity for SilverLake pilot

Thanks for looping me in. Quick product read: 1) Activation matrix = mapping "tenant tier" -> {model variant, rate limits, routing priority, cache TTLs}. 2) Tenant affinity = sticky routing to a warm pool or reserved instance set. Both are doable, but with different effort levels.

Options (tradeoffs):
- Minimal config-driven approach (LOW effort, shipable as an API + Console toggle): let Sales attach metadata to the account and route by simple rules. No per-tenant warm-pool guarantee, but we can implement priority queuing and pre-warm triggers. ETA: 3 weeks (can align to pilot start if we slot it now).
- Medium scope: config + lightweight warm pool affinity (pin tenant to a small reserved pool on demand). Requires capacity planning changes and autoscaler hooks. ETA: 6–8 weeks.
- Full scope: activation matrix + routing engine + console management + analytics. ETA: 12+ weeks.

Dev — do you see any blockers to a 3-week delivery if we scope this as config + pre-warm hooks (no hard affinity guarantees)? Also, we’ll want to draft acceptance criteria and a canary plan. I added a link to a short spec template: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2bSL-Activation-Proposal

Neha
Director, Product Management
Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 13:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: New: Activation matrix + tenant affinity for SilverLake pilot

Thanks — technical quick-take. The minimal config + pre-warm hooks is the safest path to hit the May 10 pilot kickoff. Implementation notes:
- Add a per-account metadata field (tenant_tier) consumed by the routing layer.
- Implement routing rule precedence: tenant_tier -> route to (shared pool | priority queue | reserved pool).
- Pre-warm trigger: when tenant_tier==enterprise, trigger a short-lived pinned instance and pre-populate KV cache for frequent prefixes. This is a stop-gap; it reduces tail latency but doesn’t offer strict SLAs.

Estimated work: 3 backend engineer-weeks + 1 infra week for temporary reserved pool orchestration + small Console work to expose a toggle. If Product signs off on the acceptance criteria and we get a sprint slot in April, we can deliver the minimal approach by May 6 (internal canary by May 3).

Risk: capacity contention during heavy global traffic windows — we need a fallback policy to avoid impacting other customers. Suggest we include a safe fallback config in the acceptance criteria.

Dev
Senior Software Engineer — Serving Runtime

Priya —

Good news: Product and Eng have proposed a pragmatic path we can slot in April to meet a May 6 delivery for the minimal acceptance bundle (config-driven activation matrix + pre-warm trigger). Key points:
- Redwood will deliver the config API + Console toggle and the pre-warm hook by May 6, with an internal canary May 3.
- This is explicitly a pilot-scoped capability: it provides priority routing and pre-warm behavior but does not provide firm latency SLAs for all edge cases. We will add a full affinity/reservation feature in the Q3 roadmap (ETA end of June for a stronger affinity implementation).
- Acceptance criteria: (1) ability to set tenant_tier per account; (2) routed requests for tier=enterprise hit the pre-warm path 90% of the time in canary; (3) documented fallback behavior under capacity pressure.

Next steps: Irene — can you please confirm we can include this acceptance wording in the SOW so SilverLake can move the PO forward? Priya / Procurement — if this scope is acceptable I’ll ask Legal to add the pilot acceptance gates to the SOW and propose a delivery milestone.

Tessa
Account Exec — Strategic Customers
Redwood Inference
